model.title: No new trial heats; Republican field cleanup
model.summary: The forecast leaves its general-election outlook and existing nomination probabilities unchanged because no new trial heats arrived and the latest comments about Vance and Rubio do not clearly favor one over the other. It removes Nikki Haley, who has ruled out a 2028 bid, and assigns Don Bacon a small chance after reporting that he is weighing a run and plans to take his message to early states.

overview.summary:
The forecast favors the Democratic nominee in 2028, projecting about 300 electoral votes with a plausible range of roughly 220 to 380 and a national popular-vote lead of about 4.5 points. Democrats enter the cycle after a strong 2026 midterm, winning the national House vote by about 13 points and leading 228 seats to 121 with 86 still uncounted. Arizona, North Carolina, Nevada, Georgia, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin all lean narrowly toward Democrats, with Arizona within half a point, while Ohio and Texas lean Republican by roughly 6.5 and 7.5 points.

National conditions are mixed. Presidential net approval stood at about -25 on November 19, and unemployment was 4.1 percent in October, while reports describe inflation running hotter than expected. National general-election polling has not produced a measurable 2028 shift, and a possible third-party candidacy would have little expected net effect. The forecast's uncertainty remains wide given the long time horizon and an unsettled field.
overview.watch: The next developments to watch are formal declarations from leading contenders, including Newsom's expected early-January decision, and any new general-election trial-heat polling that could shift the national picture.
key_factors: Democratic midterm strength, with a national House vote margin of about 13.5 points and broad statewide gains, including in Texas and Georgia
Deeply negative presidential approval, at about -25 net as of November 19
Mixed economic signals, with 4.1 percent unemployment in October and reports of hotter-than-expected inflation
Several battleground states clustered near even, with Arizona, North Carolina and Nevada leaning narrowly Democratic
A possible third-party candidacy whose expected net effect on the national margin is close to zero

nominations.D: The Democratic contest remains wide open, with Harris, Newsom, Buttigieg, Ocasio-Cortez and Ossoff among the leading contenders in recent polling and no candidate clearly ahead.
nominations.R: Rubio leads or is competitive in recent Republican polling, with Vance and DeSantis also in contention, while Trump has praised both Rubio and Vance without clearly favoring either.

storylines.title: Democrats post a sweeping 2026 midterm result
storylines.detail: Democrats won the national House vote by 13.29 points and made broad statewide gains, including strong results in Texas and Georgia. Florida remained a Republican outlier relative to the national House result, and the forecast retains its national shift and limited Florida-specific adjustment.

storylines.title: Approval and economic signals point in different directions
storylines.detail: Presidential net approval was -24.8 on November 19, slightly lower than its -23.7 reading on November 1. October unemployment was 4.1%, reports described hotter-than-expected inflation, and the economic index remains unavailable.

storylines.title: The Democratic primary remains wide open
storylines.detail: Recent polling shows a varied field, with Harris, Newsom, Buttigieg, Ocasio-Cortez, and Ossoff among the leading contenders. Newsom expects to decide on a run in early January, and a PAC is recruiting Buttigieg; no new general-election trial heats have arrived.

storylines.title: Shapiro's reelection and groundwork strengthen his case
storylines.detail: Shapiro's reelection, large margin, federal PAC, and reporting about his post-election groundwork keep him in the 2028 conversation. Recent primary polling remains mixed, and the forecast continues to assign him a modest nomination chance.

storylines.title: Ossoff remains a leading Democratic possibility
storylines.detail: Ossoff's Georgia victory and strong results in several recent primary polls keep him in the leading group of Democratic contenders. The polling supports a meaningful nomination chance but not a broader change in the general-election outlook.

storylines.title: A fluid GOP contest features Rubio, Vance, and DeSantis
storylines.detail: The broader primary average favors Vance, while recent polling has Rubio competitive or ahead; DeSantis is reported to be considering a run. Trump recently praised both Rubio and Vance, but the comment does not clearly favor either, and no new general-election polling warrants a forecast change.

storylines.title: AOC's team activity and new backing add to 2028 signals
storylines.detail: A progressive group has launched an effort to draft Ocasio-Cortez, and New York socialists have urged her to run; recent reporting also describes her team activity as she weighs a 2028 decision. These signals stop short of a declared campaign, and her nomination odds remain near their prior level.

storylines.title: Wes Moore leaves open the possibility of a 2028 bid
storylines.detail: Moore has said he is still sorting out whether to run, and recent reporting links his reelection to growing presidential speculation. The forecast retains his small nomination probability while the field remains fluid.

revisions.title: Rubio gains modestly after new succession signal
revisions.summary: The model modestly raises Marco Rubio’s Republican nomination chance after a new report characterized the president’s remarks as a succession signal, drawing the increase from Other. No new general-election polls have arrived, so the national outlook, state adjustment, candidate effects, and uncertainty remain unchanged; Nikki Haley is omitted because she has ruled out a 2028 run.

revisions.title: Buttigieg organizing adds a small Democratic nomination bump
revisions.summary: The model modestly raises Pete Buttigieg’s Democratic nomination chance after allies launched a PAC to recruit him, funding the increase from Other. The national outlook, state adjustment, candidate effects, and uncertainty remain unchanged because no new general-election polls or other evidence warrants a revision.

revisions.title: Wes Moore added to broad Democratic field; outlook holds
revisions.summary: The model adds Wes Moore at a small nomination probability after he said he is still considering a 2028 bid, with the probability funded from Other and the lowest-probability listed Democratic slot. No new general-election polls or other evidence warrants a change to the national outlook, state adjustments, or uncertainty; Nikki Haley is removed from the Republican list because she has ruled out a run.

revisions.title: No new trial heats; nomination outlook holds
revisions.summary: The forecast makes no numerical changes because no new general-election trial heats have arrived since the previous update, and the evidence does not justify shifting the national outlook or uncertainty. Nikki Haley remains excluded from the Republican nominee list because she has ruled out a 2028 run; her listed probability was already zero.

revisions.title: No new trial heats; national outlook holds
revisions.summary: The forecast makes no numerical changes because no new general-election trial heats have arrived since the previous revision, and the available evidence does not justify shifting the national environment or uncertainty. It retains the current nomination outlook and state adjustment while continuing to track a fluid primary season and the effects of the 2026 midterms.
